summary.text: This opportunity briefing explores combining the PC constraint-based causal discovery algorithm with predictive modeling for simultaneous causal network inference and forecasting. While causal discovery methods often reconstruct interaction networks without regard to whether the inferred structure supports prediction, pure predictive models are treated as black boxes. By leveraging high-recall candidate skeletons from constraint-based discovery and refining them through predictive performance, the framework achieves high-fidelity network reconstruction and robust system forecasting.

target_user.text: The target users are derived from academic assignee categories in the patent literature and open-source practitioners utilizing time-series causal discovery and predictive coding repositories such as causal-ts and pyhgf.

jtbd.text: When practitioners analyze complex observational time-series data, they want to simultaneously infer the underlying causal network structure and forecast system dynamics, so that they can avoid black-box predictions and understand which interactions drive the system.

value_prop.text: Unlike standard approaches that treat causal discovery and prediction as isolated tasks or black-box forecasters, this combination uses predictive modeling to prune false positive edges from constraint-based skeletons, thereby improving causal graph accuracy and delivering transparent system forecasts.

riskiest_assumption.text: Given the viability score of 1.0, the riskiest assumption is that enterprise customers will pay for an integrated causal discovery and prediction framework rather than relying on separate open-source tools or single-purpose forecasting models.

mvp.text: Conduct structured customer interviews and a price acceptance test with data science leaders to evaluate willingness to pay for combined causal network inference and forecasting capabilities, using a mock workflow as a visual aid.
mvp.type: customer interviews and price acceptance test

success_metric.text: At least a proposed threshold of 40 percent of interviewed prospective users confirm a willingness to adopt and pay for the integrated solution at a proposed threshold price of $500 per month.

kill_criteria.text: Fewer than a proposed threshold of 15 percent of interviewed customers express interest in paying for combined causal discovery and prediction over existing standalone methods.

to_build.text: A gating and refinement module that bridges constraint-based edge skeletons with predictive performance metrics to prune false positives.
